What is a Mixture?

A Mixture is formed by combining two or more substances without changing their individual properties.

What is Allegation?

Allegation is a shortcut technique used to determine the ratio in which two different values should be mixed to obtain a desired average.

Why does the average always lie between the two values?

Because the final mixture is created only from those two values.

It cannot exceed the higher value or become lower than the smaller value.

When should the Rule of Allegation be used?

When

- Two values are given.
- Required average is given.
- Mixing ratio is required.

What is Weighted Average?

Weighted Average considers both

Value

and

Quantity.

It is used whenever quantities are unequal.

Why is Water considered free in Milk and Water problems?

Because water is assumed to have no cost in standard aptitude questions.
